subject: Anchoring + burst escrow proposal for prioritized Q1 deals
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Anchoring + burst escrow proposal for prioritized Q1 deals

Team —

Quick proposal ahead of the weekly fleet sync tomorrow: Acme AI and two other Q1-target accounts are asking for predictable burst capacity and an SLA uplift if we anchor them into reserved commitments. Finance has signaled they want an escrow-style carveout (pre-allocated but billed only when consumed) to reduce revenue recognition risk.

Summary ask: approve a short-term escrow pool of 200 GPU-slots (mixed v100/A100 equivalents) that can be assigned to high-touch deals for a 90-day window. The intention is to:
- Give sales a guaranteed burst runway for pre-close pilots
- Lock in a minimum commit (for billing teams) while minimizing long-term capacity exposure

Key points in the attached matrix (escrow_matrix_v1.xlsx):
- Proposed split: 120 slots reserved for ACME / top-priority, 40 slots for Opportunity B, 40 slots for Opportunity C
- Billing model: escrow held as an availability credit; consumed tokens billed at normal usage rates; unconsumed escrow released after 90 days
- Fallback: automatic downgrade to burst queue with 24h notice if pool not available

Asks for this thread:
1) Sales: confirm the list of deals that should be eligible for the escrow pool (I’ve seeded with Acme AI).
2) Finance: temp approval for the escrow accounting treatment (Marissa).
3) Infra/Ops: feasibility and ephemeral pool provisioning timeline (Karthik / Hiro) — can we guarantee 200 slots for 90 days starting 2026-08-01?

I’ll walk through the matrix in tomorrow’s sync but wanted to get feedback and any redlines in advance.

Thanks —
Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: escrow_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with slot breakdown and billing scenarios)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Anchoring + burst escrow proposal for prioritized Q1 deals

Michael —

Thanks for the clear outline. Quick thoughts after skimming the matrix:
- I support the concept but suggest we reduce the pool to 140 slots initially (90 for Acme, 30 for B, 20 for C). Finance is likely to push back on a full 200 until we see committed MRR in the pipeline. See attached q1_forecast_snippet.pdf for the current close confidence levels that motivated this ask.
- We should include an explicit SLA table for anchors (latency targets, burst window, and an exception clause if infrastructure maintenance conflicts with burst windows).
- Please add a column for expected ARR delta per account in the sheet — will make it easier to justify to finance.

If Infra can confirm a soft allocation approach (non-preemptive during business hours for these accounts) I’ll champion a limited escrow pilot with Marissa.

Onward —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Partnerships & GTM | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: q1_forecast_snippet.pdf (3-page snapshot of weighted pipeline)

Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Anchoring + burst escrow proposal for prioritized Q1 deals

Sounds reasonable. From sales-finops side I support a scaled pilot (140 slots) and then iterate.

Infra — can you confirm whether the 140-slot soft carve can be accommodated without impacting current reserved customers? If yes, include an ETA for automated routing and a communication plan for customers that might be moved to burst queue.

Short on time this morning — will recap in the fleet sync, but please flag if any blockers.

—Ben

Subject: Re: Anchoring + burst escrow proposal for prioritized Q1 deals

Hi Michael —

Appreciate the proactive plan. Acme is interested in the 90-day pilot and the SLA uplift you mentioned. A few things from our side:
1) Can you provide a short summary of how burst billing would appear on our invoice (line item and sample calculation)?
2) We need SOC2 attestation and an ops contact for a short security review — can you share that?
3) If the escrow triggers only at heavy pilot loads, can we request a 6-hour advance notice before any downgrade to burst queue?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week to walk through details — I’m available Thu/Fri afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Sara Lang
VP of Engineering | Acme AI
sara@acme.ai

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Anchoring + burst escrow proposal for prioritized Q1 deals — infra feasibility

Folks —

Quick infra check after digging into pool topology:
- We can provision a soft-allocated pool of 140 effective slots starting 2026-08-01 for a 90-day pilot. That assumes mixed GPU types and an ops SLA that allows preemption outside business hours.
- Risks: high-day concurrency (sustained >75% utilization across the pool) will require throttling rules to avoid impacting reserved customers. We’ll provide automated routing with a 6-hour advance downgrade notice option (matches Acme's ask).
- ETA for automation and routing tests: 10 business days from approval (we’ll need a short change freeze window to apply policy changes). See attached pool_plan_v3.pdf for topology and failover steps.

Next steps:
1) Confirm final slot counts (Michael / Laura) so we can lock pool config.
2) Marissa — finance note needed for the provisional escrow accounting treatment.
3) Michael — if Acme signs limited pilot terms, provide the DocuSign link and we’ll schedule the routing rollout.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Ops | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: pool_plan_v3.pdf (network/topology and automated routing checklist)
